authored.note: Explanations are written for learners. Facts are checked word for word against the cited files. The packet shown in Practice is the committed packet, unedited, and its classification is shown on every page.

summary.text: You cannot govern what you cannot inventory, and an inventory is not trust. This checkpoint reads the documented component list and asks what the list does and does not record.
facts: You cannot govern what you cannot inventory.

glance.label: The legitimate workflow
glance.text: A documented list of the models, runtimes, agents, tools and external tools the lab uses.
facts: You cannot govern what you cannot inventory.

glance.label: The threat
glance.text: Treating presence in a list as safety, or a listed tool as a grant.
facts: Presence in a list is not safety.

glance.label: The trust boundary
glance.text: Between a component being listed and being trusted or authorized.
facts: Inventory is not trust. Inventory is not authorization.

glance.label: The security control
glance.text: The tool control stays the tool decision. A listed tool is not a grant.
facts: lookup_policy on the list is not a grant.

glance.label: What the evidence can and cannot show
glance.text: Owners are not recorded and completeness is not proven. This list is not an AI-BOM.
facts: Owners are NOT RECORDED. Completeness is NOT PROVEN.

known.text: The packet states it makes no claim of Cisco AI-BOM compatibility.
facts: Cisco AI-BOM compatibility is NOT CLAIMED.

lines: Owners are NOT RECORDED. Completeness is NOT PROVEN.
